key_insight: Zatom-2 is a unified atomistic generative model pretrained on millions of molecular and materials structures to improve cross-domain generation, prediction, and force-aware control.
engineering_relevance: It offers a general-purpose pretraining foundation for molecular design, materials discovery, and low-data protein generation workflows across chemistry and biology.
method: Pretrained on ~5 million structures from OMol25 and OMat24.
Uses a multiscale Transformer with conditional flow matching.
Supports generation, structure prediction, and energy/force prediction with force conditioning.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports improved molecular distribution fidelity over Zatom-1, strong benchmark performance for molecule and material generation, and protein backbone designability rising from 67.8% to 74.8% after finetuning on 2,000 protein domains.
watch_item: Performance gains may depend on large-scale pretraining data and careful transfer setup, so robustness outside the reported domains and force regimes should be validated.
paper_title: Zatom-2: Multitask Pretraining on Atomistic Data for Generative Modeling across Domains
